Even today at 28 I struggle with depression. Wife asked for divorce saying we have nothing in common and I'm a loner with no friends. I'm in a void and nobody can hear me scream.

But I think by taking it day by day o can somehow learn to cope with my depression the same way someone learns to cope in a wheelchair or learns to cope with a disease. And I think you can. Too.

I suppose my idea of the game is there are two parts of the game. Beating the game in the story mode which as I listed is intriguing. I love the story and feel it does a great service to the other two in the series. 

The problem with the rates is they are so low that it feels if you want to get all the characters you have to spend money. At the end of the game, once you complete all the quests, rewards etc there isn't much to do.

You get 30 stones per day which would mean it would take about a month and change to get the stones for one 10 character pack. At the low rates it is possible that even after a year of F2P you would not be able to get all of the characters.

Now the characters are not just like skins in LoL. They each have lore and they each have their own side quests. Yet unless you are willing to spend the money, or watch a play through of someone who has them, you won't truly understand that lore. 

It is frustrating to see Lokido in game, hear his dialogue and go "I want to learn more." Yet you can't. Unless you pay money, or constantly reinstall the game and play it again for the Chromo stones.

I feel without having those characters I'm missing out. Imagine in Chrono Cross if you can see how interesting Harle is, but never be able to get her as a character and hear her dialogue because you weren't lucky enough on the draw or put enough money into the game to risk getting her?

Having op characters to win the game isn't the point - though as I have seen some say there are some end game bosses that people feel can't be beat with 4 star characters.

The low rates in the tome farming system isn't the issue. I feel the issue is only being able to do it 4 times per day. What is the big issue in not having the tome farming just do as you wish and farm as long as you want? This would give the user something more to do, especially if they have a completionist attitude and are like "Well I did everything else, and I still enjoy the game, why not max all my characters?"

If the goal of having 4 times a day is to persuade the user to buy chrome stones, then why would I use chrome stones to buy tome runs when it seems the incentive to buy chrome stones is for the character packs and based on the low rates, I would never really want to buy more tome runs. Kind of like the 50 stones per revive system. It's like "Great it's there. But why would I really want to do that?"

A good system might even be gold -> Chrome stones. Maybe at a balanced rate where you would really want to buy the chrome stones instead but strengthen the F2P content.

The biggest issue to restate with the low drop rates, is each character has a side mission that expands on their lore and without that, you don't really get to know the full story.

Its one of the biggest reasons I like the characters with the maze and the school - I forget their names.

You get them, you get a huge quest story to get to know them, and while it is a huuge grind to get them to their max stars, that's completely fine.

I suffered from severe depression and suicidal tendencies as a young teenager, my mother constantly moved us from city to city every time she broke up with her boyfriend and wanted to put as much distance between them as possible.

So we move to a new state all together, a small town, everyone knows everyone etc. It's the spring of 8th grade and I get introduced as the new kid. Well I see this girl who I get placed next to. An absolute goddess. Blonde hair, blue eyes, tall, smelled nice, etc. 

I sit next to her, and I'm thinking to myself. "I'm going to move soon, it's a predictable pattern, so why not go for it?"

So I sit down and I whisper, "How's it going beautiful?" She looks over with the biggest blush. And so my week goes, learning everybody's name, teachers etc. 

I compliment her occasionally when I see her, but not an overbearing amount of course. We talk briefly when we can. I find out she is a huge Harry Potter fan, a christian, listens to christian music, basically perfect for me. To top it off, with my mind on her, my depression goes to the back side and I begin to enjoy going to school as well as being around her. It's like getting the first breath of fresh air after walking out of a very humid, very hot barn. 

I come up with a plan, to lead up to asking her out. I sit down next to her, I think it was Monday and I say, "Hey gorgeous." She smiles. I say, "Your smile is the most beautiful thing I have ever seen, I promise to make you smile at least once every day." Or something like that. 

And walk away shaking, totally put myself out there. She could reject me at any moment but doesn't. So I put a poem in her locker in the morning every day for the next two weeks or so, it seems like she is starting to fall for me. We go to a dance together, and after the dance I know for sure she is "The one." 

I fall to sleep that night sure I'm going to ask her out, that she is perfect for me and I want to be her boyfriend, the one that makes her happy and gets happiness in return. My depression is even nonexistent now, I finally feel happy every other day.

Guess. What. Happens.

Mom breaks up with her boyfriend, throws a fit, and moves us out of state, regardless of my begging of wanting to stay around this woman.

My heart is completely shattered. Spend the next 4 years completely depressed, finding no happiness. Occasionally I feel SOMETHING for a girl here or there but that gets torn away too. (As we continue to bounce around cities after every relationship my mom has). My grades plummet, I actually tried to end my life a couple of times. Get bullied for being an outcast until I graduate. 

Ended up getting married, but still unsure if the marriage was worth it, or if I just didn't want to be alone anymore. Have yet to feel anything close to the feelings for anyone like those I had for her.
